quote: In his 1545 book \emph{Ars Magna}, Gerolamo Cardano asked for two numbers that add to 10 and multiply to 40.
problem: This text sits in a `didyouknow` environment (used three times, with `% DYK-BEGIN/END` markers). The bible's fixed environment list does not include it, so it may not compile. Its historical dates are also neither checked nor cited.
fix: Remove the three `didyouknow` boxes, or fold the history into ordinary prose or an allowed environment. Keep them only if the coordinator confirms the environment exists in the preamble.

quote: \caption{Partial sums of the exponential series for $e^{i\pi/3}$.}\label{tab:complex-partial}
problem: The table uses `\begin{table}[H]`, which needs the `float` package. That package is not in the bible's list and may not be added. A float inside the `sample` box (likely a tcolorbox) will also fail.
fix: Replace the table float with a non-floating `\begin{center}\begin{tabular}...\end{tabular}\end{center}` inside the sample and refer to it as "the table below". Alternatively move the table float outside the sample with `[htbp]`.

quote: The zeros of zeta have $\sigma=\tfrac12$ and heights $t=t_n$.
problem: This states the Riemann hypothesis as fact and ignores the trivial zeros. The bible forbids implying RH is true. The same slip appears in "on the line where the zeros sit" and "the real part shared by every zero $\rho_n$".
fix: Write: "All the nontrivial zeros used in this book (numerically verified to lie on the line) have $\sigma=\tfrac12$ and heights $t=t_n$; whether every nontrivial zero does is the Riemann hypothesis, which is open (Chapter~\ref{ch:zeta})." Soften the two parallel phrases the same way.

quote: for an infinite product this also needs a convergence argument, which Chapter~\ref{ch:explicit-formula} supplies
problem: The Euler product converges only for $\Re s>1$. On the critical line, where it is used, there is no convergence argument; Chapter 18 is contracted to explain that the step is formal. The sentence promises rigor that does not exist and does not say where $s$ is.
fix: Say: "valid for $\Re s>1$, where the product converges (Chapter~\ref{ch:zeta}); on the critical line the product does not converge and the formula is only formal/heuristic, as Chapter~\ref{ch:explicit-formula} discusses honestly."

quote: Sec.~IV reports that the sparse control C2 ``recovers frequencies at $\log p^m$''.
problem: The quoted phrase is from the paper's abstract, not Sec. IV. Sec. IV says every selected frequency "lies within half the Fourier resolution of the training window of the logarithm of a prime power". Problem 16 repeats the misattribution ("The paper's Sec. IV calls such frequencies $\log p^m$").
fix: Attribute the quote to the abstract and paraphrase Sec. IV accurately, including the "within half the Fourier resolution" qualifier. Fix the parenthetical in Problem 16 to match.

quote: Both are proved in Chapter~\ref{ch:series} and in~\cite{rhb}.
problem: The chapter promises that Chapter 3 proves several things outside its contract: free rearrangement of absolutely convergent series, a rearrangement counterexample, and the Cauchy-product proof of $e^ze^w=e^{z+w}$. Chapters are written in parallel, so these promises may be false.
fix: Phrase these as taken on trust with only the textbook citation, e.g. "absolute convergence is defined in Chapter~\ref{ch:series}; the rearrangement theorem and the Cauchy product are proved in~\cite{rhb}". Do not assert what Chapter 3 proves beyond its contract.

quote: Chapter~\ref{ch:series} also shows that $e^{\mathcal S(x)}=1-x$
problem: Chapter 3's contract is only the Taylor series of $\log(1-x)$ and its radius of convergence. It need not prove the series for complex $x$, nor that its exponential equals $1-x$. The "becomes a theorem" argument rests on an unverifiable promise.
fix: Put the complex-$x$ statement $e^{\mathcal S(x)}=1-x$ for $\abs x<1$ in a `beyond` box with a textbook reference. Say only that Chapter~\ref{ch:series} derives the real series.

quote: Because complex numbers cannot be ordered (Section~\ref{sec:complex-plane}), the paper matches perturbed eigenstates to unperturbed ones
problem: The paper gives no such reason for overlap matching. It matches by overlap to identify which perturbed state descends from which unperturbed state (it reports 3% of states cannot be matched one-to-one). Sorting by real part would be possible but would not track identity. Section 3 makes the same claim.
fix: Rephrase in both places: "Complex eigenvalues have no natural 'increasing order', and in any case order does not tell which perturbed state came from which unperturbed one; the paper identifies states by overlap (Sec. II E (iii); Chapter~\ref{ch:non-hermitian})". Do not attribute the motivation to the paper.

quote: Along a path that avoids zeros, a continuous argument exists, is unique up to a constant $2\pi k$
problem: Existence of a continuous argument is asserted in the Key Ideas but never proved. The text proves only uniqueness and additivity and describes unwrapping informally.
fix: Add a short existence argument: on short enough sub-intervals $f$ stays in a half-plane, where a rotated principal argument is continuous; patch the pieces by adding multiples of $2\pi$. Otherwise put existence in a `beyond` box.

quote: differentiating real and imaginary parts with the product rule shows $\frac{\dd}{\dd t}e^{kt}=k\,e^{kt}$
problem: The computation is asserted, not shown, although it is used at once for the velocity and acceleration of circular motion. This breaks the no-skipped-steps rule.
fix: Show the lines: real part derivative $\alpha e^{\alpha t}\cos\omega t-\omega e^{\alpha t}\sin\omega t$, imaginary part derivative $\alpha e^{\alpha t}\sin\omega t+\omega e^{\alpha t}\cos\omega t$. Then verify that the sum equals $(\alpha+i\omega)e^{\alpha t}(\cos\omega t+i\sin\omega t)$.

quote: The quadratic formula works for complex coefficients too, provided we interpret the square root
problem: This is asserted without derivation. The reader knows the formula only for real numbers, and the following sample relies on it for complex roots.
fix: Add the completing-the-square derivation, $az^2+bz+c=a[(z+b/2a)^2-D/4a^2]$. Note that it uses only field algebra valid for complex numbers, and that $w^2=D$ has the two solutions $\pm i\sqrt{\abs D}$ when $D<0$.

quote: each such term is the imaginary part of a complex power $p^{-ms}$
problem: This is imprecise. By the chapter's own oracle-term equation the term equals $-\frac1m\Im[p^{-ms}]$ at $\sigma=\tfrac12$, not the imaginary part itself.
fix: Write "each such term is, up to the factor $-1/m$, the imaginary part of a complex power $p^{-ms}$ evaluated at $s=\tfrac12+it$".

quote: isolated zeros are a theorem covered in~\cite{titchmarsh}
problem: Isolation of zeros is a theorem about analytic (holomorphic) functions, a notion the chapter never introduces. "A typical complex function" is misleading, since $f(z)=\Re z$ vanishes on a whole line. Titchmarsh's zeta book is not the natural source for this general theorem.
fix: Put it in a `beyond` box: "for analytic functions (those with a complex derivative, such as polynomials, $e^z$, and zeta) that are not identically zero, zeros are isolated; see the complex-variables chapters of~\cite{rhb}." Mention $\Re z$ as a non-analytic counterexample.

quote: Problem~7 asks you to carry out the expansion for a concrete case.
problem: The general associative and distributive laws are left as "expand both sides and compare". Problem 7 checks only one numerical instance of associativity and nothing about distributivity.
fix: Show the distributive law in two lines in the text. Either show the associativity expansion or make Problem 7 ask for the general proof of both laws.

quote: Such operators have complex eigenvalues, and App.~A step 11 uses
problem: This overgeneralizes. The paper's PT-odd class has $A_{nn}=0$ and a real spectrum to leading order.
fix: Write "Such operators can have complex eigenvalues (the PT-odd class has a real spectrum to leading order, Sec. II E), and App.~A step 11 uses ...".

quote: of Sec.~III keeps ``power spectrum kept exactly'' while destroying arithmetic content
problem: The spliced quotation is ungrammatical ("keeps 'power spectrum kept exactly'").
fix: Write: "of Sec.~III is described as ``power spectrum kept exactly, no arithmetic content''".

quote: \arg k^{-s}=-t\log k\ (\text{mod }2\pi)
problem: The notation "mod $2\pi$" is never defined. Earlier the chapter only says "up to a multiple of $2\pi$".
fix: At first use (the Key Ideas of the polar-form section, or here) add: "(mod $2\pi$) is shorthand for 'up to adding an integer multiple of $2\pi$'".

quote: $3.732051=2+\sqrt3=\tan75^\circ$, so the argument is $75^\circ=5\pi/12$
problem: The value $\tan75^\circ=2+\sqrt3$ is not a standard first-year fact and is asserted without derivation.
fix: Add the derivation: $\tan(45^\circ+30^\circ)=\frac{1+1/\sqrt3}{1-1/\sqrt3}=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{\sqrt3-1}=2+\sqrt3$. Or evaluate $\arctan(3.732051)\approx1.308997$ numerically.

quote: \text{(since $w\bar z=\overline{z\bar w}$ by Eq.~\eqref{eq:complex-conjrules})}
problem: This step also needs $\overline{\bar w}=w$, which is never stated.
fix: State after the definition of the conjugate that $\overline{\bar z}=z$ (two reflections), and cite it here: $\overline{z\bar w}=\bar z\,\overline{\bar w}=\bar z w$.

quote: Raising $p^{-s}$ to the $m$-th power ($m=1,2,3,\dots$) gives, by Eq.~\eqref{eq:complex-pms} with $k=p^m$ (or by De Moivre)
problem: The equality $(p^{-s})^m=p^{-ms}=(p^m)^{-s}$ is not justified. It needs $(e^w)^m=e^{mw}$ (repeated exponent law) and $\log p^m=m\log p$. De Moivre covers only the unit-modulus factor.
fix: Insert: "$(p^{-s})^m=(e^{-s\log p})^m=e^{-ms\log p}$ by applying the exponent law $m-1$ times, and $m\log p=\log p^m$, so this equals $(p^m)^{-s}$."

quote: Unlike ordinary beats between two tuning forks, this sum never repeats exactly.
problem: The contrast is false in general. Two tuning forks with an irrational frequency ratio also never repeat exactly. What matters is whether the ratio is rational.
fix: Write: "Unlike beats between two frequencies in a whole-number ratio, this sum never repeats exactly."

quote: built from six families of rotating arrows $p^{-ms}$, $p\le13$
problem: The paper never lists the six primes. Problem 14 correctly hedges ("the natural reading is the first six"), but this paragraph states it as fact.
fix: Write "six families of rotating arrows $p^{-ms}$ (presumably the first six primes, $p\le13$; the paper says only 'six-prime')".

quote: \prob{1}{Evaluate $e^{i\pi}$, $e^{i\pi/2}$, $e^{2\pi i}$ and $e^{-i\pi/4}$ in the form $a+bi$.}
problem: The problems are not in graded order. Difficulty-1 and difficulty-2 problems (26, 28, 29) come after the difficulty-3 problems.
fix: Move this problem into the opening block of level-1 problems and move Problems 26 and 29 before the level-3 problems. Then renumber the answers and the in-text references to Problems 7, 16, 22, 23, 25 and 27.

quote: \includegraphics[width=0.95\linewidth]{figs/complex_rotation.pdf}
problem: The bible's figure template fixes `width=0.85\linewidth`. This figure and `complex_pminus_s` use 0.95.
fix: Change both to `width=0.85\linewidth`, with the scripts using figsize (6.5,3) for the two-panel layout.
